title: Career roadmap · Policy Advisor (DST/NITI)
summary: Build from research and evidence synthesis into science, technology and innovation policy, with strong capability in program evaluation, technology assessment, public-sector strategy and policy implementation.

facts.Timeline assumption: The roadmap assumes a 2026-start Ph.D. pathway. The first years focus on policy research, quantitative analysis and Indian STI institutions; later years build government-facing advisory, program-management, technology-assessment and strategic-policy leadership capability.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Become strong in STI policy research, economics, quantitative evaluation, technology assessment and Indian public-policy institutions.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Develop a policy niche such as emerging technology, R&D funding, innovation systems, deep tech, energy, health, digital technology or industrial policy.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Lead cross-ministry policy programs, evidence reviews, technology assessments and strategic initiatives.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Advise on national technology strategy, frontier science, innovation finance, regulation and long-term competitiveness.

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Retain enough technical depth to challenge scientific and engineering claims while becoming stronger in economics, regulation, public finance, institutional design and stakeholder management. Senior policy advisors must turn uncertain technical evidence into practical choices without overstating what the evidence proves.

Career progression

Ph.D. Researcher → STI Policy Researcher → Policy Analyst/Scientist → Senior Policy Advisor → Principal Policy Advisor → Policy Program Director → Director/Adviser in DST/NITI ecosystem → Senior National STI Policy Advisor

items: 15+ years, with substantial variation by recruitment route and institution
blocks.label: Typical planning ranges are

blocks.text: Ph.D. routes

A senior STI policy advisor should be able to work across scientific evidence, economics, regulation and government strategy. Maintain enough technical expertise to evaluate frontier technologies while developing strong capabilities in public finance, institutional design, geopolitical technology competition, research evaluation and implementation. The long-term goal is to advise on choices where evidence is incomplete, resources are limited and policy consequences are large.
